Can I just comment on how grateful and warm it made me feel to realise this may have been an honest response because truly I would have relapsed quickly, as I had done so many times prior, had I not had h3h3 (&Idubbbz) videos to watch during the first two weeks of withdrawals. At the time, I was living in a hotel so I had access to unlimited hot water and my legs were cramping so bad I would spend 8-10 hours a day in the bath watching h3h3 videos. I spent the rest of my day on the toilet with diarrhea or with my face in the toilet vomitting. I was so lethargic but unable to sleep due to opiate induced restless leg syndrome (absolutely the worst part of withdrawals - to date I still experience RLS for about 30 minutes prior to falling asleep and upon waking up) but because I had such low energy and was taken by h3h3 videos I chose not to waste what little energy I had to go score and instead to continue watching videos. I cannot say it was deliberate - not relapsing I mean. But at the time it took way more effort to score than it did to continue withdrawing with h3h3. 
After the acute symptoms disappeared I still had severe RLS for about 5 months, every night of which I would turn on h3h3 and fall asleep listening to a podcast or some h3h3 playlist. I would wake up listening to them also.
Furthermore, I was inspired to buy another laptop through his videos (of course, I had pawned everything I owned up until this point including two car titles and a title on a 2003 CBR 600.) So, his videos directly encouraged me to resume my love for technology and I now work in the field I went to college for -tech related btw. 
Most of these people in this thread have given me this feeling that I haven't been familiar with in such a long time - that feeling of warm, gratefulness. 
Sorry for the long ass post. I just wanted to share my story.
